subject: Data Engineering
title: Dead Letter Queues
description: A fast breakdown of Dead Letter Queues for builders.

hook.text: A malformed event crashes the consumer on every retry. The entire stream stalls.

buildup.text: Some events can't be processed no matter how many times you retry. They're poison pills.

discovery.text: A dead letter queue catches unprocessable events, routing them aside so the main stream keeps flowing.

twist.text: Dead letters aren't trash. They're evidence. Reviewing them reveals bugs, schema issues, and edge cases.

climax.text: Every production streaming system needs a dead letter queue. It's insurance against the unknown.

punchline.text: Don't let one bad event block the whole stream.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a dead letter queue?
options: To capture unprocessable events so the main stream keeps flowing
